cities.base: The Barkhor, in one of the Tibetan courtyard hotels within five minutes of the Jokhang; it is 3,650 m and you spend the first two days here doing very little, so being able to walk to tea and dinner w
cities.name: Lhasa

cities.base: Yingxiong Road by the dzong, the Yeti Hotel or the Gyantse Hotel, both a ten-minute walk to the Kumbum and the old town lane; one night is right, arriving in the afternoon from the Yamdrok road.
cities.name: Gyantse

cities.base: The old town under the dzong, within a walk of Tashilhunpo's gate and the Qingdao Road market; the new Chinese city to the east is where the good hotels are and the worst evenings.
cities.name: Shigatse

cities.base: Rongbuk Monastery guesthouse or the yak-hair tent camp beside it at 4,980 m: a bed with an electric blanket, a stove, a shared pit toilet and no running water, the tents standing only from late April
cities.name: Rongbuk (Everest Base Camp)

cities.base: Naidong Road around the Tsedang Hotel, the only quarter with restaurants, 12 km from Yumbulagang and 40 km from Samye; at 3,100 m it is the lowest bed of the trip and the right place to end.
cities.name: Tsedang

cities.base: No beds worth using; Nagarze on the far shore has truck-stop rooms at 4,400 m. You see the lake from the Kamba La pass and the shore on the road day between Lhasa and Gyantse, and that is the right wa
cities.name: Yamdrok Lake (Kamba La)

cities.base: No beds; a 4,300 m ridge 50 km east of Lhasa reached in 80 minutes by car or on the pilgrim bus, done as a half day from the Barkhor.
cities.name: Ganden Monastery

cities.base: Do not sleep here: the Tashi Dor guesthouses are at 4,720 m and are shut in winter. It is a long day from Lhasa over a 5,186 m pass, five hours each way, and only worth it on a ten-day trip if you dro
cities.name: Namtso

cities.base: There is a monastery guesthouse, but sleep in Tsedang and come for the morning; it is an hour by road from Tsedang and about the same from Lhasa on the new highway.
cities.name: Samye Monastery

places.name: Potala Palace
places.note: Your guide books a timed slot the day before on the official WeChat account, you clear security 30 minutes early, and you then get a hard one hour inside across thirteen storeys of stairs at 3,700 m, so do it on your third morning, not your first; 200 CNY May to October, 100 CNY November to April.

places.name: Jokhang Temple
places.note: Pilgrims have the Jowo chapel in the early morning and in high season tourists are let into the inner chapels from late morning, so arrive around noon, do the chapels clockwise and finish on the roof for the Potala view; 85 CNY.

places.name: Barkhor kora
places.note: Clockwise only; one lap is twenty minutes and the real one is at dusk when the prostrators and the juniper burners are going, and the shops on it sell nothing you cannot buy cheaper a street back.

places.name: Sera Monastery and the monk debate
places.note: The debate runs 15:00 to 17:00 Monday to Saturday in the walled courtyard and never on Sunday or festival days, so be inside by 14:00 to see the chapels before they shut and to get a spot on the low wall; 50 CNY.

places.name: Drepung Monastery
places.note: Go in the morning while the Ganden Palace and the Tsokchen chapels are open and the light is on the white buildings; the kora above it is an hour and gives the whole Lhasa valley, and Nechung, the oracle's seat with the darkest murals in Lhasa, is a ten-minute walk downhill; 60 CNY.

places.name: Tibet Museum
places.note: Free, rebuilt in 2022, shut Mondays and last entry 16:30; the thangka, manuscript and mask rooms are good and the political framing is what you would expect, so read it as context and move on.

places.name: Norbulingka
places.note: The Dalai Lamas' summer palace park, a flat easy walk for the first afternoon while your head is still adjusting; the 1950s Takten Migyur palace with the murals of Tibetan history is the one building worth the queue; last entry 17:30.

places.name: Tromsikhang market
places.note: Yak butter cut from slabs, dried cheese, tsampa and hanging meat in the market behind the Barkhor's north side; go before ten when the butter sellers are busy and you want to smell Lhasa rather than see it.

places.name: Guangming Gangqiong sweet tea house
places.note: Long benches, sweet milk tea poured from a kettle for a few mao a glass and Tibetan noodles at 8 to 10 CNY; you leave coins on the table and the pourer takes what is owed, and it is the least staged hour you will have in Lhasa.

places.name: Lhasa Kitchen
places.note: Tibetan and Nepali menu at around 60 CNY a head opposite the Jokhang square; yak momos, tsampa soup and the yogurt are the order, and it is where the guides eat, which is the point.

places.name: Tibetan Family Kitchen
places.note: A family flat turned restaurant a lane off the Barkhor's south side; book the evening momo and noodle cooking class for the night you have nothing else, about 80 CNY a head to eat and roughly 150 for the class, and it is still full of reviews from summer 2026.

places.name: Makye Ame
places.note: The yellow building on the Barkhor corner sold on a Sixth Dalai Lama story; the food is average, the bill is double Lhasa Kitchen's and the tour buses fill it, so use it for one rooftop drink at most.

places.name: Kamba La pass viewpoint
places.note: The turquoise lake from the pass is the reason the road exists, and it is also where the men with dressed-up yaks and mastiffs charge 20 to 50 CNY for a photo you did not ask for; ten minutes, no fee for the view, and do not run up the steps at 4,794 m.

places.name: Yamdrok lakeshore below the pass
places.note: The road drops 400 m from the pass to the water and the first pull-off on the shore is where you can actually walk to the lake, which the pass cannot give you; twenty minutes on the stones and back in the car.
places.neighborhood: North shore, on the Nagarze road

places.name: Samding Monastery
places.note: The seat of Tibet's only female incarnate lama, on a hill over the lake's south arm 10 km before Nagarze; a 20-minute detour with a small ticket, a few monks and nuns, and a view of the lake without a single vehicle in it.

places.name: Pelkor Chode Monastery and the Kumbum
places.note: The Kumbum's nine tiers hold seventy-odd chapels of 15th-century Newari-influenced murals and you climb them clockwise, chapel by chapel; some halls shut 13:00 to 15:00 so it is a morning job, 60 CNY in and 10 CNY more for interior photos.
places.neighborhood: North end of the old town

places.name: Gyantse Dzong
places.note: A steep twenty-minute climb at 4,000 m to the fort the British shelled in 1904, with an anti-British museum inside and the best view of the Kumbum and the old town grid; go late afternoon when the light is on the monastery; 30 CNY.

places.name: Gyantse old town lane
places.note: The cobbled lane from the dzong gate to the monastery is one of the last intact Tibetan town streets, whitewashed houses with cattle in the yards and prayer flags on the roofs; walk it before nine when the cows are going out.
places.neighborhood: Between the dzong gate and the monastery

places.name: Pelkor Chode wall ridge walk
places.note: The monastery's perimeter wall climbs the ridge behind it and you can walk up along it for the view down onto the Kumbum's roof and across to the dzong; 150 m of climbing, loose in places and empty.

places.name: Pala Manor
places.note: A pre-1959 aristocratic manor kept as a museum with the family rooms and chapel upstairs and the servants' cells below; it is propaganda and it is also a real house, and both halves earn an hour.

places.name: Gyantse Tibetan carpet factory
places.note: Gyantse has woven carpets for centuries and the small state workshop lets you watch the looms without buying; if you do buy, a metre-square rug is a few hundred dollars and they ship.

places.name: Tsechen Monastery ruins
places.note: A wrecked hilltop monastery-fortress with one rebuilt chapel and a 30-minute climb that gives the whole Nyang Chu plain; free, nobody there, and the roadside village below is where the yak dung is drying on the walls.
places.neighborhood: Hill 5 km north on the Shigatse road

places.name: Karola glacier
places.note: A glacier tongue hanging over the road at 5,020 m on the way in from Yamdrok; the 50 CNY viewing platform is the deal, the costumed yaks are not, and the ice has retreated a long way up the mountain since the photos on the sign.
places.neighborhood: Karo La pass, 70 km east on the Lhasa road

places.name: Simila pass and the Manla reservoir
places.note: The last pass before Gyantse with the reservoir a hard blue below; five minutes of photos, prayer flags, no fee, and the only stop where nobody sells you anything.

places.name: Tashi Restaurant
places.note: Nepali-run with an English menu, curries, yak sizzlers and pizza at 50 to 60 CNY a head; it is the default for every foreign group in town and still the best meal you will get in Gyantse.

places.name: Tashilhunpo Monastery
places.note: Seat of the Panchen Lamas, with the 26 m gilded Maitreya and the tombs of the fourth and tenth; the chapels shut for lunch 12:00 to 14:00 so start at nine, photos inside cost extra per chapel, and it is 100 CNY May to October, 55 CNY in winter.

places.name: Tashilhunpo kora
places.note: Three kilometres round the outside of the walls, climbing behind to the giant thangka wall for the roofs and the whole town; pilgrims do it before eight and so should you, then go in when the gate opens.
places.neighborhood: The path round the monastery walls

places.name: Shigatse Dzong
places.note: A 2007 concrete rebuild of the fort the Potala was modelled on, empty inside, but the stairs up are free and give the town, the monastery and the Nyang Chu plain in twenty minutes.
places.neighborhood: The hill north of the old town

places.name: Old town and the Qingdao Road market street
places.note: Stalls under the dzong selling prayer flags, knives, butter and cheap Chinese goods, the free market of old guidebooks in a tidier form; bargaining still starts at a third.

places.name: Shalu Monastery
places.note: A 14th-century monastery with Mongol-period green glazed roofs and Newari murals that nothing else in Tibet looks like; a one-hour detour off the road in from Gyantse, about 40 CNY, and usually empty.

places.name: Narthang Monastery
places.note: The ruined walls of the printing monastery whose woodblocks produced the Tibetan canon, with one rebuilt chapel and a few monks; a 30-minute stop on the morning you leave for Everest, not a destination.
places.neighborhood: Narthang village, 15 km west on the Everest road

places.name: Gang Gyen carpet factory
places.note: A working carpet workshop a few minutes from the monastery gate where you watch the weavers and are not pressed to buy; a good half hour to fill while the chapels are shut for lunch.

places.name: Shigatse Wordo Kitchen
places.note: Braised yak ribs, curried potatoes and a Tibetan song set at about 70 CNY a head; the music is for visitors, the kitchen is the best Tibetan one in town, and the English-speaking staff are real.

places.name: Third Eye Restaurant
places.note: Nepali-run with a patio, dal bhat and yak curry at 50 to 60 CNY and proper vegetarian choices; the lunch stop while Tashilhunpo's chapels are shut, and confirm it is open before you walk over, since Shigatse's foreigner restaurants come and go.

places.name: Tashi Restaurant
places.note: Tandoori, Nepali and Indian at around 50 CNY a head above the old town; cheaper than Third Eye and the one locals send you to when Songtsen, the old favourite, is shut, which it has been for stretches since 2021.

places.name: Rongbuk Monastery
places.note: The highest monastery there is, a few monks and nuns in a rebuilt shell with the north face of Everest filling the valley behind the chorten; the chapels open when someone is there to open them, and the light on the mountain is what you came for.

places.name: Everest Base Camp, the 5,200 m platform
places.note: The 180 CNY park ticket and the 120 CNY eco-bus get you to the marker stone at 5,200 m, which is as far as tourists go now; the face is 20 km away and fills the sky, the wind is constant, and you walk 300 m from the bus, not more.
places.neighborhood: Tourist base camp, 4 km beyond Rongbuk

places.name: Rongbuk chorten at sunrise
places.note: Everest goes pink from the top down about twenty minutes before the sun reaches the valley, and the chorten with prayer flags in front of the monastery is the frame everyone uses; dress for minus ten even in June.

places.name: The night sky from the tent camp
places.note: At 5,000 m with no town for 100 km the Milky Way is a wall and Everest is a black cut-out under it; ten minutes outside is all most people manage, and a headache in the morning is normal.

places.name: Tent guesthouse dinner
places.note: Thukpa, fried rice, sweet tea and a yak-dung stove in the tent you sleep in, 20 to 30 CNY a plate; the tents stand from late April to early October and the guesthouse canteen at the monastery does the same food the rest of the year.

places.name: Rongbuk Monastery guesthouse canteen
places.note: Noodles, rice, fried dishes and instant food at the monastery guesthouse, open all year when the tents are down; eat lightly, drink more tea than you want, and expect nothing to taste of much at this altitude.

places.name: Gawula pass
places.note: The first sight of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu and Shishapangma in one line from the pass above the 108 hairpins; fifteen minutes on the platform is enough, and the afternoon cloud usually takes the summits after one.
places.neighborhood: Gawula, 5,198 m, on the Shegar road

places.name: Shelkar Dzong and Shekar Chode
places.note: The ruined fort walls climb the crag above the small monastery in Shelkar, the town most people sleep in before or after Rongbuk; an hour's scramble for the view and a rebuilt chapel below.

places.name: Tashi Dzom village
places.note: The last real village before the monastery, with a few Tibetan restaurants doing yak momos and noodles and Sichuan stir-fry; the lunch stop on the way in, and 800 m lower than Rongbuk if you need a bed off the mountain.
places.neighborhood: Tashi Dzom, 4,200 m, on the Rongbuk road

places.name: Old Tingri Everest view
places.note: A truck-stop town on the Nepal road with Everest and Cho Oyu on the southern skyline from the edge of the plain; worth the 60 km detour only if you are going on to Kyirong, otherwise see it from Gawula.

places.name: Gyatso La pass
places.note: The highest point of the Friendship Highway and the first time most people feel 5,000 m; a gate, prayer flags, a glimpse of Everest on a clear day, and ten minutes before the headache starts.
places.neighborhood: Gyatso La, 5,220 m, between Lhatse and Shelkar

places.name: Sakya Monastery
places.note: A grey fortress-monastery with red and white stripes, the 13th-century seat of the Sakya school, with a library wall of 10,000 manuscripts behind the main hall; 50 CNY, open 09:00 to 18:30, and it costs the day two hours of driving, which it earns.
places.neighborhood: Sakya town, 25 km off the Everest road at Lhatse

places.name: Yumbulagang
places.note: The first palace in Tibet, a 1980s rebuild on a rock spur above the Yarlung fields, 20 minutes of steps or 30 CNY on a horse; the chapels are 60 CNY, the ridge above the palace is free and gives the whole valley, and mornings are calm before the wind.

places.name: Trandruk Monastery
places.note: A 7th-century temple with the pearl thangka of Chenresig, some 29,000 pearls on silk, in an upstairs chapel; 70 CNY, on the road to Yumbulagang, and often only the caretaker is there.

places.name: Tombs of the Tibetan kings, Chongye
places.note: Ten grass mounds in a side valley hold the empire's kings, Songtsen Gampo's the biggest with a small chapel on top; the climb gives the valley and Riwo Dechen monastery, and you will have the place to yourself.

places.name: Mindroling Monastery
places.note: The main Nyingma monastery of central Tibet, in a side valley off the Tsangpo road with a 13-storey chorten and murals of Padmasambhava; a one-hour stop on the drive from Lhasa, and the small teahouse by the gate does butter tea.
places.neighborhood: Dranang valley, 45 km west on the Lhasa road

places.name: Tsedang old town and Ganden Chokhorling
places.note: The Tibetan lanes behind the Chinese main street, with a small 14th-century monastery and butcher and barley shops; the only part of Tsedang that is not new, and half an hour is right.

places.name: Gangpo Ri and the Monkey Cave
places.note: A pilgrim path climbs the hill where a monkey and an ogress supposedly bred the Tibetan people, to a shrine cave at about 4,000 m; 400 m of ascent, two to three hours, and Tsedang and the Tsangpo below you the whole way.

places.name: Rechung Phuk hermitage
places.note: Milarepa's disciple Rechungpa's cave in a small rebuilt monastery on a spur, 20 minutes up from the road between Trandruk and Chongye; free, a handful of monks, and the best view over the Yarlung fields.
places.neighborhood: Ridge between the Yarlung and Chongye valleys

places.name: Tashi Restaurant
places.note: The Tsedang branch of the Nepali-run chain, English menu, curry, pasta, yak steaks and a proper bacon breakfast at 50 to 60 CNY; the safe dinner in a town with few options for foreigners.

places.name: Aba Home Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Family-run Tibetan with photos on the menu, yak with radish, potato momos and butter tea at around 50 CNY; where your guide will eat if you let them choose.

places.name: Yi Wan Mian noodle shop
places.note: A bowl of hand-pulled noodles or a clay-pot of dumplings for 15 to 20 CNY with a bilingual menu; the lunch that takes twenty minutes on the way back from Yumbulagang.
places.neighborhood: Near the PSB office, Naidong Road

places.name: Samye Monastery
places.note: Tibet's first monastery, 8th century, laid out as a mandala with the three-storey Utse temple in the middle in Tibetan, Chinese and Indian styles; 40 CNY, the chapels are open 09:00 to 16:00 and the upper floors go dim after three, so it is a morning.
places.neighborhood: Samye, north bank of the Tsangpo

places.name: Hepo Ri
places.note: The hill where Padmasambhava is said to have subdued the local gods, 150 m of climbing in 30 minutes for the mandala plan of Samye laid out below with the river and the dunes behind; the only way to see the monastery as it was designed.
places.neighborhood: The hill east of the monastery

places.name: Chimpu hermitage
places.note: Meditation caves and stone huts up a side valley where nuns and hermits still live, a rough 40-minute drive then an hour's climb at 4,000 m; free, quiet, and the one place near Lhasa where the religion is not a museum.
places.neighborhood: Chimpu valley, 10 km north of Samye

places.name: Ganden Monastery
places.note: Tsongkhapa's own monastery on a horseshoe ridge above the Kyichu, flattened in the 1960s and half rebuilt, with his tomb chapel and the assembly hall; 50 CNY, opens at seven in summer and the pilgrim bus from Lhasa gets there by nine.

places.name: Ganden high kora
places.note: Three and a half kilometres over the back of the ridge to 4,400 m with sky-burial sites, rock paintings and the Kyichu valley 700 m below; do it before the monastery so the climb is done while you are fresh, and take the 2 km low kora if your head hurts.

places.name: Tashi Dor peninsula
places.note: Two rock hills on the shore with a small monastery, caves and a one-hour kora round the base, and the lake going to the horizon with the Nyenchen Tanglha range behind; 210 CNY in season including the mandatory park bus, 145 in winter, and it is cold in any month.

places.name: Lakenla pass
places.note: The pass above the lake at 5,186 m, the highest point of the whole trip, with the first view of the water; five minutes, prayer flags, and back in the car before your head notices.
places.neighborhood: Lakenla, 5,186 m, on the road in

outings.why: Sunrise at the Rongbuk chorten, then the eco-bus 4 km up to the 5,200 m marker and a short walk to the face; three hours from Rongbuk, seven if you slept in Shelkar and drove in. The hard part is being at 5,200 m at all, and the cloud usual
outings.name: Everest Base Camp from Rongbuk
outings.season: All year; tents late April to early October, and the road ca
outings.fallback: If cloud sits on the face, take the eco-bus anyway for the glacier moraine and turn round; the north face is often clear again at dusk.

startsFrom.name: Rongbuk Monastery guesthouse or tent camp

outings.why: 350 km and two 5,200 m passes, with the Himalayan panorama from Gawula and the 108 hairpins down to Tashi Dzom; nine hours door to door with lunch at Lhatse and the park gate paperwork at Shelkar. Leave by eight so you are on Gawula before
outings.name: The Everest road: Shigatse to Rongbuk over Gyatso La and Gawula
outings.season: All year; heaviest snow risk December to February and cloud
outings.fallback: Stop at Shelkar for the night and drive the last 90 km to Rongbuk at dawn.

outings.why: The 260 km road day: over Kamba La at 4,794 m for the lake, down to the shore, past Nagarze and up to the Karola glacier at 5,020 m, then Simila and into Gyantse by mid afternoon. Everyone does it and it is still the best road in central Ti
outings.name: Kamba La, Yamdrok and Karola to Gyantse
outings.season: All year; Kamba La can close for a morning in snow between D
outings.fallback: Take the flat Tsangpo valley road to Shigatse instead and see Gyantse as a day trip from there.

outings.why: 80 minutes out to the ridge, the 3.5 km high kora to 4,400 m with the Kyichu valley below, then the monastery; back in Lhasa for a late lunch. The climb is short but it is the first time you work at 4,300 m, so do it on day three, not day t
outings.name: Ganden and the high kora
outings.season: All year; the kora is icy at dawn December to February.
outings.fallback: The 2 km low kora and the monastery only, four hours door to door.

outings.why: 250 km each way over Lakenla at 5,186 m to the lake at 4,720 m, two hours on the peninsula, and the same road back; eleven hours, most of them in the car, and the pass is higher than base camp. Only for a trip with a spare Lhasa day after R
outings.name: Namtso and Tashi Dor
outings.season: May to October; the pass closes for snow the rest of the yea
outings.fallback: Yangpachen hot springs and the Nyenchen Tanglha view from the Damxung road, six hours.

outings.why: An hour to the monastery, two hours in the Utse and the outer temples before the upper chapels go dim, then 30 minutes up Hepo Ri for the mandala from above; five hours from Tsedang, six from Lhasa. Add Chimpu and it is a full day.
outings.name: Samye and Hepo Ri
outings.fallback: Samye alone, three hours, if the wind on the dunes is up.

outings.why: Trandruk's pearl thangka on the way out, the steps up to Yumbulagang and the ridge above it, then Rechung Phuk or the Chongye tombs on the way back; a morning at 3,600 m on the flattest ground of the trip.
outings.name: Yumbulagang, Trandruk and the Yarlung valley
outings.fallback: Yumbulagang only from the car park, two hours.

outings.why: The wall path with the pilgrims before eight, then the Maitreya chapel and the tombs from nine until the halls shut at noon; four hours in the town itself, and the reason Shigatse gets a night rather than a lunch stop.
outings.name: Tashilhunpo and its kora
outings.fallback: The monastery alone, two hours, if the kora is iced.

destination.name: Tibet
destination.pitch: The best-run high-altitude road trip there is if you accept the terms: a licensed guide beside you every hour, three nights in Lhasa before you go anywhere, and one cold night at Rongbuk under the north face of Everest before you drop back
destination.caveat: A licensed Tibetan guide and an agency vehicle are compulsory from the moment you land to the moment you leave, the permits need a Chinese visa first and about three weeks of processing, and the second half of the trip runs at 4,300 to 5,200 m where most people feel ill for a day whatever their fitn Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Lhasa is a Chinese provincial city wrapped around a Tibetan old town of a few streets, and it is the only town on the trip with an evening.
because.food: Momos, thukpa, yak in every form and sweet tea from a kettle, done well in a handful of Barkhor kitchens and Nepali-run places, and then instant noodles at 5,000 m.
because.nature: Turquoise lakes at 4,500 m, a roadside glacier, and the north face of Everest filling the valley from a monastery courtyard at 4,980 m.
because.culture: Living Gelug monasteries with debates at three every afternoon, the Jokhang full of pilgrims before dawn, and a 15th-century Kumbum you climb chapel by chapel.
because.adventure: Two 5,200 m road passes, a night at Rongbuk and a kora at 4,400 m; nothing technical, and the altitude does all the work.
because.relaxation: Evenings are early and quiet because everyone is tired at altitude, not because anything is calm; the Barkhor at dusk is the nearest thing to a slow hour.
because.exploration: Weak, and you should know it before you book: your route is on the permit, your guide is with you at every site, and detours are negotiated the night before, though the Barkhor and the town streets are yours to walk.
